name: Plant Utilities & Auxiliary Media (Air, Water, Steam, Fuel, Inert Gas)
aliases: fuel gas / fuel oil / diesel supply
zones: compressor house / air compressor & dryer skid
cooling water pump house & cooling tower / chiller plant
instrument air receivers & drop legs to field

activities: compressor/pump/skid foundations and plinths
cooling tower basin, water treatment and tank foundations
utility pipe-rack foundations and rack steel readiness
trenches for buried cooling/raw water lines, bunds for fuel
sequence.note: Civil enters as enabler only: skid plinths, rack foundations, tank/basin civils and trenches.

activities: set air compressors, dryers and receivers
set cooling water pumps, cooling tower / chiller modules
set demin/RO trains, boilers and fuel forwarding skids
set nitrogen generation / vaporiser package
erect utility headers on pipe-racks (air, CW, steam, fuel, N2)
run branch tie-ins to each consumer battery limit
install isolation, PSVs, traps, strainers and drop legs
install insulation/tracing on steam, condensate and cold lines
power to compressor, pump and package motors
terminate field instruments (pressure, flow, level, conductivity)
connect package control panels / PLC to plant control (BMS/DCS)
flush/blow-through water lines; air-blow/dry-out air & gas lines
chemical clean / passivation of demin and boiler circuits
condensate line clean-out before steam admission
hydrostatic test of water and condensate systems
pneumatic test of compressed-air, instrument-air and nitrogen lines
steam line pressure test and controlled warm-up / boil-out
sequence.note: Gas and air headers are pneumatically (not hydro) tested to avoid trapped water in instrument-air; steam lines require staged warm-up.

activities: compressor no-load run, dryer dew-point set-up
cooling water fill, vent, circulate and treat
boiler light-off preparation, fuel system leak/purge check
nitrogen generator purity ramp and receiver charge
establish instrument-air header at pressure and dew point (first utility live)
establish cooling water circulation at design flow/temperature
raise steam and stabilise distribution / trap operation
prove fuel forwarding pressure/flow to consumers
prove nitrogen purity and supply pressure for purging/blanketing

typical_relationships.reason: Rotating utility packages are grouted to plinths that must be cast and cured first.

typical_relationships.after: Erect utility headers (air / water / steam / fuel / N2)
typical_relationships.reason: Headers are supported off the rack; the rack must exist before pipe is hung on it.

typical_relationships.after: Flush / blow-through and pressure test the utility line
typical_relationships.reason: A line can only be cleaned and pressure-tested once it is fully erected and isolatable.
Debris must be removed before the line is pressurised, or valves, PSVs and instruments foul.

typical_relationships.before: Instrument-air system commissioned (air available at pressure & dew point)
typical_relationships.after: Loop-check / stroke pneumatic control valves on any system
typical_relationships.reason: Pneumatic actuators and positioners cannot stroke until clean, dry instrument air is available.

typical_relationships.after: Run heat-generating equipment (compressors, chillers, process) under load
typical_relationships.reason: Equipment that rejects heat cannot run on load without its cooling medium flowing.

typical_relationships.before: Demin water / boiler feed available and chemistry in spec
typical_relationships.reason: A boiler cannot be fired without feedwater of the correct chemistry, or it scales and trips.

typical_relationships.after: Purge / inert hydrocarbon or oxygen-sensitive systems
typical_relationships.reason: Purging and blanketing require the inert gas to be available at the specified purity first.
Cold steam lines must be warmed and drained of condensate before load, or water hammer damages piping.

typical_relationships.after: First fire of any fuel-burning equipment
typical_relationships.reason: A fuel train must be proven leak-tight and purged before ignition for safety.

interfaces.requirement: Permanent power to compressor, pump and package motors before any utility can be run and made available.
Instrument air must be commissioned first because it enables loop-checking / valve stroking across every other system.
Cooling water, air, steam, fuel and nitrogen must be available before process equipment can be commissioned or run on load.
Skid foundations, pipe-rack foundations, tank/basin civils and bunds complete before setting packages and erecting headers.
Utility header and consumer tie-in piping erected and tested before the utility is declared available.
Utility header pressures, temperatures and status published to plant control for downstream commissioning dependency checks.
Steam, condensate and hot/cold utility lines insulated (and traced where required) before sustained operation.

testing_requirements: Hydrostatic test of water, condensate and cooling systems
Pneumatic test of compressed-air, instrument-air and nitrogen headers
Steam line pressure test plus controlled warm-up / boil-out
Cooling water flow balance and chemistry establishment
Demin / boiler feed water conductivity and chemistry in specification
Nitrogen purity (ppm O2) verification at delivery point
Fuel system leak test and purge / inerting verification before first fire
commissioning_dependencies: Permanent power to utility rotating equipment and packages
Utility distribution piping erected, cleaned and pressure-tested
Instrument air established first as the enabler for control valves plant-wide
Water source (raw / treated) available to fill circuits
Package control panels integrated with plant control (BMS/DCS)
System punch clearance permitting energisation and pressurisation
typical_exceptions: Instrument-air and nitrogen headers are pneumatically tested, never hydro-tested, to keep them dry
A site with utility-supplied medium (e.g. district steam, municipal water) may omit on-site generation but still needs distribution tie-in and test
Nitrogen may be bottle-bank/vaporiser supplied on small plants instead of an on-site generator
Closed-loop cooling with chillers replaces open cooling towers on some plants, changing the fill/treatment steps
evidence: A downstream system (process equipment, control-valve loop checks, boiler firing) is scheduled to commission before its enabling utility — instrument air, cooling water, demin water, fuel or nitrogen — is itself erected, tested and made available.
